battery_overview: The Strategic Interpretation Battery is Call 7 — the client-facing strategy layer that sits above the three analytical batteries (Epistemic Motion, Forensic Analysis, Semantic Content). It receives the output of one battery at a time, strips all evidence fields, and interprets the findings through a declared client bias. The client specifies their side, witness posture, primary concern, desired finding, feared outcome, and opposing counsel read. Call 7 then produces a strategic brief: what to use, what to watch, how the calls rank in importance for this pair, a two-to-three word strategic signature, and value scores for both sides. Three separate Call 7 files are produced per pair — one per source battery.

client_bias_declaration.note: Call 7 is not neutral. The analysis is always shaped by six declared inputs from the client: (1) which side they are preparing for (prosecution or defense), (2) their current assessment of the witness posture, (3) their single biggest concern about this deposition, (4) what they most hope the analysis surfaces, (5) what outcome would be most damaging to their side, and (6) their read on opposing counsel's likely strategy. These six inputs are injected into the prompt directly and define the lens through which all battery output is interpreted.
client_bias_declaration.what_you_want_to_find: Defendant failure to follow safety practices
client_bias_declaration.case_context: Cristoball Jasso v. Shell USA, Inc. and Shell Chemical, L.P. · Benjamin Gibson deposition, February 14 2025 · Direct examination by Ms. Kate Easterling for the Defense · Gibson serving as expert witness for Plaintiffs

pattern_field.label: Pair Strategic Signature
pattern_field.definition: A 2–3 word strategic label capturing what this pair means for the client's case position. Derived from the client's declared perspective after reading all battery output. Distinct from the pattern declarations produced by the analytical batteries — those label epistemic or forensic events; this labels strategic consequence.
pattern_field.scale: Qualitative (2–3 word phrase) · always client-perspective · strategic, not analytical
pattern_field.why_it_matters: Names the strategic consequence of this exchange for the declared client side — what this pair means in case-position terms, not analytical terms.
pattern_field.examples: Contractor Blame Shift, Deflection Advantage, Credibility Risk, Narrative Anchor

fields.label: Summary
fields.definition: A 3–4 sentence strategic overview from the declared client's perspective. Answers: what happened in this exchange that matters to the client? What should they know before walking into or past this pair? The summary is direct and opinionated — it is a strategy brief, not a neutral description. It does not fabricate winning conditions that are not supported by the battery output.
fields.why_it_matters: Provides the strategic bottom line for this pair — the first thing a trial attorney reads when reviewing this pair's analysis.

fields.label: Pair Strategic Signature
fields.definition: A 2–3 word strategic label capturing what this pair means for the client's case position. Derived from the client's declared perspective after reading all battery output. Distinct from the pattern declarations produced by the analytical batteries — those label epistemic or forensic events; this labels strategic consequence.
fields.scale: Qualitative (2–3 word phrase) · always client-perspective · strategic, not analytical
fields.why_it_matters: Names the strategic consequence of this exchange for the declared client side — what this pair means in case-position terms, not analytical terms.

fields.label: Client Value
fields.definition: Integer score (0–10) assessing how useful this pair is to the declared client side. Scores use the full range — pairs are not clustered toward the middle. A pair can score high on both sides simultaneously if it is high-stakes for both.
fields.scale: Integer 0–10: 0 = zero strategic value · 3 = low / worth logging · 5 = moderate / actively useful · 7 = significant / act on this · 9 = critical / could move the needle · 10 = ignore at your own peril
fields.why_it_matters: Quantifies the strategic asset value of this pair for the client — enabling prioritization across the full deposition.

fields.label: Opposition Value
fields.definition: Integer score (0–10) assessing how useful this pair is to the opposing side. Independent of client_value — scored from the opposition's perspective, not the client's. A pair can score high on both sides simultaneously.
fields.scale: Integer 0–10: 0 = zero strategic value · 3 = low / worth logging · 5 = moderate / actively useful · 7 = significant / act on this · 9 = critical / could move the needle · 10 = ignore at your own peril
fields.why_it_matters: Quantifies the threat level of this pair — how much the opposition can exploit it, independent of its value to the client.

fields.label: Use This
fields.definition: Battery findings the client can actively use, ordered from most to least useful. Each item identifies: the utility level of the finding, which call produced it (1–6), which specific field within that call contains it, and a 1–2 sentence explanation of the strategic value to the declared side. Evidence must be drawn from the battery output — not invented or inferred from the original transcript.
fields.scale: Ordered array of {utility: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high', source_call: integer 1–6, source_field: field name, reason: text (1–2 sentences)}
fields.why_it_matters: Converts analytical findings into actionable strategic assets — the specific things the attorney can use from this pair.

fields.label: Watch This
fields.definition: Battery findings that represent risk or threat to the declared client's side, ordered from highest to lowest threat. Each item identifies: the threat level, which call produced it, which field contains it, and a 1–2 sentence mitigation strategy. Watch This items are not symmetrical to Use This — the opposition's advantage is not necessarily the client's threat unless it is actionable against them.
fields.scale: Ordered array of {threat_level: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high', source_call: integer 1–6, source_field: field name, mitigation: text (1–2 sentences)}
fields.why_it_matters: Surfaces the risks in this pair and provides mitigation strategies — what the attorney needs to watch out for and how to prepare.

fields.label: Call Rank
fields.definition: All six calls from the source battery ranked 1–6 by strategic importance for this specific pair on the declared side. Rank 1 is the most strategically important call; rank 6 is least important. The ranking reflects the value of each call's output for the client's position on this pair — not the general importance of the call across all pairs. Each item includes a one-sentence explanation of the ranking.
fields.scale: Array of {call: integer 1–6, rank: integer 1–6, reason: text (1 sentence)} · all six calls must appear · no ties
fields.why_it_matters: Directs the attorney to the most strategically valuable analytical output for this pair — where to focus attention first.
